step1_summary: Chief complaint: Left-sided throbbing headache for ~24 h

History of present illness: Began on waking yesterday; constant baseline with intermittent worsening. Described as intense, throbbing, photophobia present. No nausea, vomiting, visual change, aura, abnormal smells/tastes, rhinorrhoea, fever, neck stiffness, focal weakness, numbness. Pain a little better when lying in dark; not related to posture, cough or Valsalva.
Past medical history: None reported. No previous headaches.
Medications/allergies: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) for 6 yrs; paracetamol taken for pain. Allergy: aspirin (causes marked nausea). No regular NSAID use.
Family history: Mother – hypertension and migraine.
Social history: Lives with friends. Alcohol: moderate (weekends). Non-smoker. No recreational drugs.
Vital signs / exam: None recorded (telephone consult). Patient denies feeling febrile; no focal neurological deficits reported; no skin rash.
Labs / imaging: None performed or mentioned.

V: Subarachnoid haemorrhage – sudden severe unilateral headache could represent sentinel bleed, though intensity described as ‘quite painful’ rather than ‘worst ever’; photophobia fits.
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – new headache in young woman on oestrogen-containing OCP; may present with unilateral throbbing pain and photophobia.
I: Viral (aseptic) meningitis – headache and photophobia without marked systemic illness can occur early.
Acute bacterial meningitis – needs exclusion despite absent fever/neck stiffness.
Acute sinusitis – can cause unilateral headache, worse with light sinus pressure.
N: Intracranial neoplasm (e.g., meningioma, glioma) – new progressive unilateral headaches, photophobia possible.
Pituitary adenoma – can present with new headache in 30-year-old woman.
D: Tension-type headache – stress trigger, bilateral or unilateral pressure pain possible.
Cervicogenic/musculoskeletal headache – worsens with posture, relieved lying, stress-related.
I2: Medication/analgesic-overuse headache – frequent paracetamol but only one day makes this unlikely.
OCP-induced migraine – combined pill can precipitate new migraine.
C: Cerebral arteriovenous malformation – may cause new headache or bleed in young adult.
A: Migraine without aura – classic unilateral throbbing, photophobia; family history strongly supportive.
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudo-tumour cerebri) – photophobia and headache in young women, but classically worse lying flat.
T: Post-traumatic headache – no recent trauma reported.
E: Hypertensive headache – OCP user with possible undetected hypertension.
Hypoglycaemia/Metabolic derangements – patient eating normally, unlikely.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, moderate–severe intensity, relief in dark, family history of migraine, common demographic (female, 30 s), no red-flag neurologic signs.
Stress at work, first episode, pain fluctuates rather than paroxysmal, no nausea/vomiting; tension headache can be unilateral and photophobia is possible, though less typical.
Young woman on combined OCP, new persistent unilateral headache; CVST often presents sub-acutely without focal deficits early on.
Headache with photophobia could be early meningitis, but absence of fever, neck stiffness or systemic symptoms make it less likely.
Needs exclusion in any acute unilateral severe headache with photophobia, but onset not described as sudden ‘thunderclap’ and patient able to converse comfortably after 24 h.

supporting_evidence: Moderate–severe intensity, worsens with routine activity/light
No previous similar headaches but stress is a recognised trigger
opposing_evidence: No prior personal migraine history (first presentation at 31 yrs)
Pain does not completely resolve between attacks (continuous baseline)

supporting_evidence: Pain present all day with fluctuations
No vomiting, aura, or focal neurology
opposing_evidence: Described as throbbing rather than pressure/tight band
Photophobia more typical of migraine than tension headache

supporting_evidence: Female on oestrogen-containing OCP (major risk factor)
Photophobia can occur with raised intracranial pressure
opposing_evidence: No focal neurological deficits, seizures, or papilloedema reported
Onset not progressive over days to weeks; only 24 h so far
No mention of recent infection, dehydration, or pregnancy that further increase risk

supporting_evidence: No antibiotic/antiviral pretreatment that would mask fever
opposing_evidence: No fever, neck stiffness, myalgia, nausea or vomiting
Feels generally well; eating and drinking normally
Not described as ‘worst ever’ thunderclap; onset seemed gradual on waking
Able to carry out conversation 24 h later without deterioration
No neck stiffness, vomiting, or loss of consciousness
